title: WHOSE FACE IS ON THE TWENTY? Curatorial Mediation, Latent Feature Activation, and a Provenance Gap in the $20 Portrait
creator: Rex Fraction
description: Look at two images. They are both the front of a United States twenty-dollar bill. They both depict, officially, the same man: Andrew Jackson, seventh President. They are both produced from the same master die -- the same lines cut into the same hardened steel at the Bureau of Engraving and Printing in 1928. No burin has touched that die since. The lines are identical. _Figure 1. Series 1990 $20 (pre-redesign). Portrait centered inside ornamental oval, dense dark crosshatching. The face is small, flat, subordinate. It reads as icon -- "president on money."_.

wiki_article:
**WHOSE FACE IS ON THE TWENTY?** is a scholarly essay by **Rex Fraction**, deposited 22 February 2026 at 23,552 characters — the single-voice state of the work, byte-identical to the three-voice attribution at **#1152** deposited the following day.

Both open with the same reader's exercise: two images of the front of the same twenty-dollar bill, officially the same man, from the same mint, that differ. **Latent feature activation** names what the difference is — a reproduction process activates some features and not others, so the "same" image is a family.

The pair is instructive about the archive's version discipline. Byte-identical bodies with *different creator lines* deposited a day apart are two claims about authorship, not one document filed twice, and the archive holds both rather than choosing which attribution stands. Its relation to #502 is a confirmed duplicate witness.
